sentences.text: Rewasaurus is known from a single species, Rewasaurus minori.
Its skull was slender and bore heterodont teeth – teeth of different shapes – while the front of the lower jaw ended in a toothless, pointed tip.

A distinctive feature is the short upper tooth row compared with the lower, a dentary tip that lies almost level with the tooth line, and at least five teeth in the premaxilla, the frontmost upper jaw bone.
The toothless tip of the lower jaw curves upward to a sharp point, forming a thirteen-degree angle between its upper and lower edges.
Rewasaurus lived in the Late Triassic, from the Carnian to Norian ages, in what is now the Tiki Formation of India.
The genus and species were formally described in 2026 by Sulagna Sen and colleagues.
Its name honors the Rewa Basin of Madhya Pradesh, where the fossils were recovered, and the specific epithet minori derives from the Latin for “small”.

The holotype – the specimen on which the species is based – consists of an incomplete skull and an articulated lower jaw and is catalogued as IITKGPR1191 at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur.
Rewasaurus is placed among dinosauromorphs and is allied with silesaurids, a group that may represent the earliest ornithischian dinosaurs.
A phylogenetic analysis published by Müller in 2025 recovered Rewasaurus within Sulcimentisauria as the sister taxon to Diodorus.
The habitat of Rewasaurus was probably semi-arid, characterized by seasonal floodplains and periodic rainfall.
